body.text: A 13-year-old boy is fighting for life being burned during the incident in Taylors Hill on Monday. ( ABC News )
In short:
Young people who allegedly carried out a firebombing at a house in Melbourne's north-west were tasked with targeting the address by middlemen who contacted them on WhatsApp.
One teenager is still fighting for life in hospital after being engulfed in flames when two cars were set alight in Taylors Hill.
What's next?
The ABC understands police will use phone data to investigate the car fire.
Link copied Share Share article A schoolboy fighting for life after setting himself alight in a botched alleged arson attack received his orders via WhatsApp, the ABC can reveal.
Vision shows two other people leaving the 13-year-old boy for dead after two vehicles were set alight on Woolwich Way in Taylors Hill , in Melbourne's north-west, on Monday morning.
The boy remains in a critical condition with severe burns to 90 per cent of his body.
The ABC can reveal the group was tasked with targeting the address by middlemen who had communicated with one another using aliases on WhatsApp in the lead-up to the incident.
After allegedly setting the two cars on fire, the trio had attempted to flee the scene in an allegedly stolen car, but crashed it seconds later.
The two others then ran away, leaving the 13-year-old on fire behind.
Police on Thursday said they had arrested three teenage boys over the incident — two 16-year-olds and a 15-year-old.
They will be interviewed by detectives.
Live Moment
Acting Commander Troy Papworth from North-West metro region provided an update on recent arson attacks across Melbourne.
Press conference wraps up
Acting Commander Papworth says Victoria Police is confident it can find the culprits further up the chain of command and arrest them.
That concludes the update on the latest arsons.

Show more Close friends of the boy, who attends a secondary school in Melbourne's northern suburbs, told the ABC they were praying he survived.
One friend, who cannot be named because they are underage, said: "He is a great guy. I felt alive with him."
Another friend told the ABC: "He is more than just a friend to us. He is someone who brought so much laughter and happiness to everyone around him.
"We have so many memories together that I'll always hold close to my heart and it would really be sad if we lose him.
" No one deserves that. He was a funny person with so much love for everyone around him. "
Two cars were destroyed in the firebombing and the Woolwich Way home was damaged. ( ABC News )
"He was always making people laugh, even when nobody was expecting it," another close friend said.
"He was caring, loyal and always there for his mates.
"We're really worried about him. We're just hoping and praying that he pulls through."
Six cars set alight outside Melbourne homes in fourth night of firebombings
It brings the number of cars destroyed across the city this week to 13.
It is understood phone data will be central to the police investigation into the arson, which is among a string of similar incidents across Melbourne over consecutive nights.
"As a result of this incident, we have a young boy whose life is currently hanging in the balance," Detective Inspector Chris Murray from the Arson and Explosives Squad said.
"We intend to hold all those who were with him responsible for his critical injuries but importantly, we are committed to identifying those who tasked this arson.
" Without their involvement, these crimes would not occur. "
Inspector Murray said criminal syndicates were using young offenders because they were easier to manipulate and "easier to replace".
"Those who start fires rarely control where they end.
"Once a fire is lit, it becomes unpredictable, uncontrollable and potentially deadly. It can end in tragedy.
"Let me be clear: this is not a game — no amount of money is worth risking your future or your life."
Multiple vehicles were torched in Springvale, Reservoir and Oakleigh East overnight .
Yesterday, homes in Balwyn North and Maidstone were damaged by fire , following arsons in Keilor and the Taylors Hill fire involving the 13-year-old.
The incident is not the first of its kind to leave Victorians with life-threatening or deadly burns.
Last month, a man in his 20s sustained what police described as "life-altering" burns while trying to torch a Melton tobacconist.
Another 52-year-old man spent almost six months in hospital before succumbing to his injuries after attacking a dessert bar in Chapel St.
Innocent woman Katie Tangey, 27, was killed when arsonists mistakenly targeted her brother's Truganina townhouse , where she had been house-sitting at the start of 2025.
